solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stop silly club maybe providing old-fashioned communication

indicators.note: something silly is not in its proper sensible order, so the preceding word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a club is one suit of playing card, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Someone tells a daft golf or social club to stop sending letters the quaint old way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a picture card through the mail is now a rather dated way of keeping in touch.

clue.text: Alexander? Alexander, maybe!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Alexander ..., the eighteenth-century English poet, known by his surname
second meaning: several pontiffs took the name Alexander, so Alexander may be one

explanation.walkthrough: The same name read twice: once as a poet's first name pointing to his surname, once as a papal title pointing to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's surname and the church office coincide, so the one word fits both readings of the name.

clue.text: Commercial event with southern beer

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for southern
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A trade promotion held in the south, with beer on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's period of reduced prices is a commercial occasion designed to draw buyers.

clue.text: Cheering arrival outside stronghold

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: an arrival is a coming
a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: Relief forces arrive outside a besieged castle, which is cheering news for those within.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheering lifts the spirits, just as consoling or reassuring words do.

clue.text: Old widow, king and priest coming to court

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible, a crossword favourite
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: An elderly widow, a monarch and a cleric all turn up at a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic noun for a widow or surviving spouse; the 'old' marks the word as dated rather than the woman.

clue.text: Loud Greek character presenting his cheese?

definitions.note: 'his' refers back to the Greek in the wordplay, so the definition leans on the whole clue

parts.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A noisy Greek man shows off his national cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet; 'his' then borrows the person reading for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The crumbly brined white cheese is traditionally made in Greece, so it is a Greek's own cheese.

clue.text: Ultimate net value looking wrong

indicators.note: if the words look wrong, their letters are out of place and need rearranging

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant's final net figure seems to be in error.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what comes at the end, the final outcome after everything else.

clue.text: Unusual woman embraced by a bishop — 50

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside the arms of what surrounds it

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for bishop
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a woman's name

explanation.surface: An odd scene: a fifty-year-old woman being hugged by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman sits between the bishop and the 50, so the embrace is by the whole run of letters, not just the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual departs from the norm, which is just what deviating from the standard means.

clue.text: Learner hiding in tree seen by everyone in London thoroughfare

indicators.note: a thing hiding in another is concealed within it

parts.note: a palm is a kind of tree
L for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A learner driver concealed behind a tree, in full view of the whole street.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall is a famous street in central London, lined with gentlemen's clubs, running near St James's Palace.

clue.text: Started losing heart and head

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word drops its central letter

parts.note: began means started

explanation.surface: Someone began to lose courage and then lost their head entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like part of the deletion instruction, but it is the definition; only the heart is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for the head, as in a blow on the bean.

clue.text: Plants found by nieces wandering across country

indicators.note: spread across something means stretched over it on both sides
letters that wander stray from their original positions

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a land is a country

explanation.surface: Wildflowers discovered by a pair of nieces rambling through the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Celandines are small yellow-flowered plants of hedgerows and woods, common in early spring.

clue.text: Stick around and see county town

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Chester is one

explanation.surface: Persevere and visit the main town of the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' reads as stay put, but 'around' turns the stick backwards; 'see' is the noun meaning a bishop's seat, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorchester is the county town, the administrative centre, of Dorset in south-west England.

clue.text: Craftsperson who could create thin mist

indicators.note: creating something new from given material suggests making a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artisan who conjures up a faint haze, like a stage magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is a skilled worker who makes and mends articles from tin plate, a traditional trade.

clue.text: What could be made more safe is frightening

indicators.note: what could be made from these words is a new word formed from their letters

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A paradox: the thing that might be made safer is itself scary.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome describes something that inspires fear, so it is a near synonym of frightening.

clue.text: Imagine one piece of fruit filled with energy!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something filled with another thing holds it inside

parts.note: a date is a single fruit of the date palm
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Picture a single piece of fruit bursting with vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea or concept in the mind, which is to conceive or picture it.

clue.text: Fruit always eaten by the old man

indicators.note: food eaten by someone ends up inside them

parts.note: papa is a word for father, and 'old man' is slang for father
ay (or aye) is an old word for always, as in for ay

explanation.surface: Tropical fruit that Dad always eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaya is a large tropical fruit with orange flesh and black seeds, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Good person cheerful or in shock?

definitions.note: here a dazed state of shock, a noun

parts.note: ST, short for saint, a very good person
up means in high spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a decent person is happy or traumatised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a choice between two states, but it is simply carried into the answer as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed near-unconscious state, the numbed condition of someone in shock.

clue.text: Source special diet for Lent season

parts.note: a spring is the source of a stream

indicators.note: a special version is a reworked one, so the next word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Finding a special diet to follow during the Lenten fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pushes 'special diet for Lent' as fasting; Lent instead stands for the time of year in which it falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Springtide is a poetic word for springtime, the season during which Lent falls; the word Lent itself comes from an old word for spring.

clue.text: Some anatomical bit that is very small

indicators.note: some of a word is just a part of it, a run of letters taken from inside

parts.note: the run of letters after the first two

explanation.surface: Describing a tiny part of the body seen in anatomy class.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, so a tiny particle or minute bit of anything.

clue.text: Architect seen as a flighty type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Christopher ..., designer of St Paul's Cathedral in London
second meaning: a small songbird, a creature that flies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests a fickle person; here it means simply able to take flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous architect's surname is also the name of a tiny brown bird, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Something charged when member finally enters club

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside what it enters

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word beside it

parts.note: the last letter of member

explanation.surface: A club member is billed when they finally join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' sounds like a society the member joins, but it is the definition, a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is one of the golf clubs with a metal head, used for mid-range shots.

clue.text: Unmarried person rests uneasily, keeping quiet at home

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within
resting uneasily means tossing and turning, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A single person sleeps badly, staying quietly at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinster is an unmarried woman, a now old-fashioned term.

clue.text: Attention given by the male journalist?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Asking whether a male reporter paid notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Heed is notice or careful attention, as in to pay heed to a warning.

clue.text: Old Labour minister: angry fellow

parts.note: cross means angry
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A former Labour cabinet member described as an irate chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Crossman was a British Labour cabinet minister in the 1960s, famous for his diaries.
